chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in his will to his son Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyah:

Know that the chivalry (muru'ah) of a Muslim man consists of two types of chivalry: one in the city (home) and one while traveling. As for the chivalry in the city, it is reciting the Quran, associating with the scholars, pondering over jurisprudence, and maintaining prayer in congregations. As for the chivalry while traveling, it is providing provisions, minimizing disputes with one's companions, and frequently remembering God, the Exalted, in every ascent, descent, sitting, and standing.

key_terms.حَضَر: Home, city, or settled life; the opposite of travel.
key_terms.مَرْؤَة: Chivalry, manliness, or virtue; a comprehensive term for noble character and conduct.
key_terms.مُجَالَسَةُ الْعُلَمَاءِ: Associating with or sitting with scholars.

ai.seo_question: What are the two types of chivalry (muru'ah) for a Muslim according to Imam Ali's will?
ai.summary: In this foundational teaching from his will to Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, Imam Ali (AS) defines 'muru'ah' not merely as physical bravery but as a comprehensive ethical framework adaptable to one's environment. The distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on balancing intellectual rigor and communal worship in settled life with spiritual mindfulness and social harmony during journeys, reflecting the holistic nature of Islamic character.
